description: Offline optimal dispatch schedule by DP, giving the cost-latency Pareto frontier a policy can be measured against. Replaces `Oracle`, which was documented as an upper bound and is beaten by hybrid at three rates.
note_n: 60 requests matches e40's trace length, so the frontier is computed on the same workload the hardware measured. The DP is exact but its state is a Pareto set per prefix, so cost grows faster than linearly in n; 60 keeps a full sweep to seconds.
note_lambda: lambda is ms of TPU cost traded per ms of summed request latency. 0 is pure cost -- maximal batching, unbounded wait -- and large lambda approaches dispatch-on-arrival. The values are geometric so the frontier is sampled evenly in the region where the curve actually bends.
note_oracle: `oracle` is included as a POLICY here, not as a bound, precisely because e30 showed it is not one.
